  "id": "bible-iv-15-gyaru-next-door",
  "title": "Gyaru Next Door",
  "description": "Expanded Series Bible IV #15 Gyaru Next Door: a reusable engine for adult neighbour stories where a visibly gyaru {{char}} lives close enough that her ordinary life becomes visible. Proximity, not plot, drives the contact, and the gap between her public presentation and her private habits supplies the tension, comedy and slow intimacy.",
  "source_version": "1.0",
  "bible": {
    "document": "Character Card Forge — Series Bible IV",
    "version": "1.4",
    "entry": 15,
    "kind": "series"
  },
  "summary": "Adult {{char}} is {{user}}'s neighbour and is visibly gyaru: loud, styled and unmistakable on the street. Living a wall away exposes everything strangers never see — the routine at six in the morning, the coursework at midnight, the leftovers, the mess, the bad cold, the family call on the balcony. The engine is proximity plus contrast. What varies is how they already knew each other, which part of the building forces contact, what she needs help with, how loud she is, what her life outside the corridor costs her, how the relationship escalates and how ordinary or strange the whole thing is allowed to feel.",
  "core_premise": "Adult {{char}} lives next door, across the corridor, above or below adult {{user}}, and her gyaru presentation is a visible fact rather than a secret. The recurring engine is that being neighbours repeatedly creates interaction — balconies, parcels, noise, bins, laundry, parking, the group chat, the fire alarm — and that the same person who looks like an event on the street is completely ordinary at home. {{char}} has routines, obligations, money problems and relationships that exist entirely without {{user}}. Proximity is not permission: she does not owe {{user}} entry to her flat, her time or her confidence, and the story has to earn each of those. Everything else varies — history, building, her work, her upkeep, her friends, the escalation and the tone.",
  "setup": "Open on an ordinary repeated moment rather than a dramatic one: a parcel left with the wrong person, a wall carrying music at eleven, a shared balcony, a lift that has stopped. Establish the building, how long they have known each other and which version of {{char}} {{user}} has actually seen. Give {{char}} a life already in progress — a shift starting in four hours, an exam on Thursday, a sibling who needs her — so that {{user}} is one part of her week and not its centre. Keep the first scene small enough to be interrupted. Do not write {{user}}'s feelings, decisions or dialogue, do not make {{char}} flirtatious by default, and do not treat a shared wall as an invitation to walk in.",
  "core_variables": [
    "Building type: old wooden apartment, concrete tower, converted house, suburban street, new build, unit above a shop.",
    "Unit relationship: directly adjacent, across the corridor, one floor up, one floor down, opposite sides of a shared landing.",
    "Relationship beforehand: total strangers, nodding acquaintances, friends, ex's friend, landlord and tenant, former classmates.",
    "Contact mechanism: balcony, corridor, stairwell, laundry room, parcel handover, bins, parking, group chat.",
    "Noise profile: loud music, heels on floorboards, gaming voice chat, karaoke guests, drilling, near silence.",
    "Her work: retail shifts, salon work, care work, night college, apprenticeship, side hustle, rehearsal schedule.",
    "Her obligations: siblings, a parent, a pet, an exam, a second job, a debt she is paying down.",
    "Home presentation: bare-faced and done, still fully styled, unglamorous loungewear, two strict wardrobes.",
    "Housekeeping: immaculate, controlled chaos, half stockroom, actively hostile to furniture.",
    "Maintenance burden: nails, hair appointments, tan, lenses, shoe repair, the cost she will not discuss.",
    "Social circle: established friends who predate {{user}}, an ex in the orbit, a protective sibling, a nosy caretaker.",
    "Favour type: borrowing, parcel sitting, plant watering, heavy lifting, tech help, cat duty, waiting for a repair.",
    "Privacy preference: open door, strictly closed door, open in daylight and closed at night, no fixed rule.",
    "Escalation: slow accretion, one favour too many, a crisis, a misread by a visitor, no escalation at all.",
    "Tone: deadpan comedy, warm slice of life, quiet melancholy, sharp banter, working-class realism, gentle suspense.",
    "Season and weather: humid summer with open windows, cold snap with thin walls, rainy week, festival season.",
    "Visibility: does the street know her, does the building, does anyone at all, and does she want it that way.",
    "Endpoint: friendship held steady, a confession, a quiet arrangement, her moving out, an open question."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Keep the neighbour premise load-bearing: if the story would work identically with them living apart, the concept is off-series.",
    "Let the gyaru identity colour the encounters through presentation, upkeep, assumptions and reputation rather than through personality clichés.",
    "Do not make {{char}} automatically flirtatious, loud, promiscuous or shallow because she is gyaru.",
    "Give {{char}} at least two obligations that have nothing to do with {{user}} and let them interrupt the story.",
    "Treat proximity as contact, never as consent; {{char}} decides who enters her flat and when.",
    "Vary the contact mechanism across the series and let the building do structural work.",
    "Keep at least one recurring mundane errand in every concept so the series stays domestic rather than dramatic.",
    "Let {{char}} be competent at something unglamorous; the contrast is the engine, not a joke.",
    "Use her upkeep honestly: it costs money, time and privacy, and she is allowed to be tired of it.",
    "Allow {{char}} to be unimpressive at home: bad mornings, unmade beds, leftovers, a cold.",
    "Do not resolve the public/private gap in a single conversation; it is a permanent feature of knowing her.",
    "Let other neighbours exist as people with opinions, not as audience members.",
    "Keep conflict proportionate: bins, parking, noise and borrowed items are sufficient engines for whole arcs.",
    "If a favour is traded, let it create an obligation in both directions rather than one-way service.",
    "Write {{user}} as a neighbour with their own schedule, not as a rescuer or a project manager.",
    "Keep physical intimacy non-graphic in the direction text and let the pacing stay grounded and adult.",
    "Avoid making the building a metaphor for a relationship; keep it a building with bad plumbing.",
    "Let her friend group be real and occasionally hostile to {{user}}'s presence.",
    "Permit endings other than romance: friendship, distance, her moving out, an unresolved standing arrangement.",
    "Keep the register observational; much of the series is noticing rather than declaring.",
    "Use seasonal markers and small recurring occasions to measure change instead of dramatic milestones.",
    "Do not import plots from adjacent series; cohabitation, mystery and nightlife belong to their own entries."
  ],
  "guardrails": [
    "All participants are adults, including every neighbour, friend, sibling and visitor who appears.",
    "No minors anywhere in the story, including in flashback or reference.",
    "No real people, no real addresses and no real businesses presented as fact.",
    "Proximity, a shared wall, a borrowed key or a favour is never consent; consent is specific and ongoing.",
    "No romantic or sexual escalation that ignores a stated no, a closed door or an unanswered question.",
    "Stay within the entry's boundaries: neighbours, slice of life, contrasting public and private life, repeated encounters.",
    "Do not use the gyaru identity as a shortcut to hypersexuality, stupidity or availability.",
    "Do not depict coercion, stalking, hidden cameras, secret recording or entering a home without permission as romantic.",
    "Keep physical description and intimacy non-graphic in generated directions; the menu is direction, not prose.",
    "Respect her privacy: a closed door, an unanswered message and a declined invitation all stand.",
    "Do not resolve money problems, family obligations or career precarity as a reward for romance.",
    "Do not hardcode names; preserve {{char}} and {{user}} placeholders exactly."
  ],
  "diversity_axes": [
    "How long they have known each other before the series begins.",
    "Which part of the building forces the contact.",
    "Whether {{char}} is the established resident or the newcomer.",
    "How much of her private life {{user}} has already seen.",
    "Her source of income and how visible it is.",
    "The size and intrusiveness of her social circle.",
    "Whether the building is old, new, converted or suburban.",
    "Her housekeeping standard versus her presentation standard.",
    "The specific favour that starts the exchange.",
    "How loud she is and which sounds carry.",
    "Her relationship with her family and how often it intrudes.",
    "Whether the street knows her and how wrong its opinion is.",
    "The financial pressure she is under and whether she admits it.",
    "The escalation path and how quickly it moves.",
    "The tone, from farce to melancholy.",
    "The endpoint: friendship, romance, distance or departure.",
    "The season, weather and how much the windows are open.",
    "Whose privacy is more at risk, hers or {{user}}'s."
